chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated to me from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning a man whom janābah has affected while he is in the open desert, and he has only one garment upon him, and his garment has been affected by semen. He said: He performs tayammum, puts aside his garment, sits with himself drawn together, then performs salat, indicating by gesture.

Thus, the proper way to reconcile the two reports is that if he is in a place where no one can see his ʿawrah, he performs salat standing; and if that is not the case, he performs salat sitting. Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb also narrated the first report with his chain, and we have mentioned it in our major book, and it says: he performs salat sitting. According to this narration, there is no contradiction between the two reports in any circumstance.

key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment, which is the only clothing he possesses
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.عَوْرَتَهُ: his private area that must be concealed
key_terms.مَنِيٌّ: semen, causing ritual impurity on the garment
key_terms.مِنْ قُعُودٍ: from a seated posture in salat
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum in place of wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable

ai.seo_question: How should a person in janābah pray if he has no water and his only garment is impure?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling for a person in a state of janābah who is stranded without water and possesses only one garment that has been soiled with semen. It explains that he should perform tayammum and pray in a manner that preserves modesty, and it reconciles apparently differing reports by distinguishing between whether his ʿawrah is visible to others or not.
